summary.text: Jared Huffman is a Democratic attorney and environmental lawyer who served on the Marin Municipal Water District board and in the California State Assembly (2006-2012) before his 2012 election to Congress. Elected Ranking Member of the House Natural Resources Committee in 2025, he is also a senior member of the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee. His stated 2026 campaign priorities, per his Ballotpedia survey, are affordability, accountability and democracy.

paragraphs.text: Born February 18, 1964, in Independence, Missouri; graduated from William Chrisman High School in 1982.
Earned a bachelor's degree from UC Santa Barbara in 1986, where Wikipedia reports he was a three-time All-American volleyball player, and a law degree from Boston College Law School.

Worked as an attorney, including as associate attorney at McCutchen, Doyle, Brown & Enersen, managing partner at Boyd, Huffman & Williams, and managing partner at The Legal Solutions Group, LLP, and as a senior attorney for the Natural Resources Defense Council from 2001 to 2006.
Was elected to the Marin Municipal Water District board in 1994 and served 12 years, including three terms as board president.

Represented the 6th District in the California State Assembly from 2006 to 2012, where he chaired the Water, Parks & Wildlife Committee and the Assembly Environmental Caucus; he was barred from a fourth term by term limits.

Entered the 2012 race for California's 2nd District after 20-year incumbent Lynn Woolsey announced her retirement, won with more than 70% of the vote according to Wikipedia, and took office January 3, 2013; he has been re-elected since.

In 2025 House Democrats elected him Ranking Member of the House Natural Resources Committee, and he is a senior member of the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, per his Ballotpedia survey response.
Co-founded the Congressional Freethought Caucus with Rep. Jamie Raskin in 2018 and serves as its co-Chair; also a Vice-Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus.
Lives in San Rafael with his wife, Susan, and their two children, according to Wikipedia.
